title: The Autobiography of St. Ignatius
author: Ignatius of Loyola (dictated to Luis Gonçalves da Câmara, 1553-1555)
translator: Edited by J. F. X. O'Conor, S.J.
edition_cited: New York: Benziger Brothers, 1900. archive.org scan stignatiusautobi00ignauoft
tradition: Roman Catholic; founder of the Jesuits
locator_hints: Chapter 'Spiritual Trials' (printed pp. 40-41; about lines 975-1000): the recurring beautiful shape 'of the form of a serpent with glittering eyes' seen at the Manresa hospital

Chapter 'Heavenly Favors' (pp. 54-58; lines 1340-1440): white object with rays; white rays at the elevation; the humanity of Christ as a white body seen twenty to forty times; the illumination by the river; recognition of the serpent-thing as diabolical and driving it off with his staff
p. 72 area (line 1800): on the voyage the visions took 'the form of something large, round, and golden'
summary: Ignatius's dictated memoir. At Manresa (1522-23), during months of long daily prayer, severe fasting, vigils and penance, he repeatedly saw a beautiful indistinct shape 'of the form of a serpent with glittering eyes, and yet they were not eyes', which gave great consolation and left sadness when it went. He also reports a white object with rays, white rays descending at the elevation of the Host seen 'with the eyes of his soul', and the humanity of Christ as a white body without distinct members, seen 'perhaps twenty or even forty times'. After the illumination beside the river he saw the many-eyed thing again near a cross, noticed it had lost colour, judged it the devil's work, and thereafter drove it off with his staff. On the voyage to Jerusalem he saw something 'large, round, and golden'.
why_relevant: First-person report of recurring seen luminous forms with the practice regime that surrounded them, a stated distinction between bodily seeing and 'eyes of the soul', and a discernment procedure that ends in rejecting one of the lights.

date_evidence.basis: title page of the saved text: 'Benziger Brothers ... 1900'; copyright line 1900

notes: O'Conor's 1900 English is a free rendering. It says the serpent-like shape appeared 'on a clear moonlight night ... in the courtyard'; modern translations of the same passage (e.g. Tylenda, Young) read differently (I recall 'in full daylight' and 'in the air near him'), which matters for the eyes-open tag. The reading agent should flag this and not rest a claim on O'Conor's wording alone. The Spiritual Diary (1544-45: tears, warmth, visions of a luminous sphere) exists in English only in in-copyright translations: see excluded/unobtained list.
